newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Akzo has high hopes for Remeron, Puregon.
newsitem.headline: Akzo has high hopes for Remeron, Puregon.

text.p: Chemical group Akzo Nobel NV said on Wednesday the launch of its new anti-depressant Remeron was expected to significantly boost operating profits at its pharmaceuticals division next year.
"We are very hopeful for this product," finance director Syb Bergsma told Reuters Financial Television in an interview.
He said that third-quarter pharmaceuticals profits had been braked by start-up costs for introducing the new drug.
"When the increasing sales...take over next year that of course will be a very healthy impact on our pharmaceutical profits," Bergsma said.
Bergsma earlier told a news conference Remeron was expected to unlock a billion guilder market.
"As you know there has been much praise (for Remeron) from psychiatrists relative to Prozac," Bergsma said.
In September, results of a trial with the drug were presented at a neuropsychopharmacology congress in Amsterdam.

Presenting the results, Professor Stuart Montgomery of London's St Mary's Hospital said they showed that "Remeron really ought to replace conventional antidepressants such as the tricyclics and SSRIs like Prozac in the treatment of depression".
Akzo also has high hopes for its new fertility drug, Puregon, Bergsma told the news conference on Wednesday.
"In time this (Puregon) could be a hundreds of million guilder market," he said.
